scope: Evidence-only independent audit of the exact-source T30 final revalidation packet retained at harness/evidence/t30/676db22-final-revalidation.
Recompute the packet checksum inventory, source-input and principal-artifact hashes, source commit/tree/digest bindings, command exit pairing, and selected raw-result summaries.
Inspect the reported Node, Chromium, lifecycle, input, heap, standalone, site, documentation-layout and installed direct-name package evidence against the T30 acceptance boundary.
No product source, test, budget, task state, lockfile or prior evidence was modified. No performance, browser, install, publication or network command was rerun in this review.

standaloneAndSite.siteRouteObservation: The retained raw site report has three routes and the requested 10 cold/30 warm samples per route; the report is observational and asserts no timing threshold.

findings.requirement: The unchanged planner p95 budget must remain reliable under the documented workload; a pass is not evidence of universal timing conformance.
findings.evidence: The two qualifying author repetitions report 13.512291 ms and 13.925833 ms p95 against 16 ms, leaving 2.49 ms and 2.07 ms headroom. The packet also retains a prior exact-a245 independent-review miss of 21.314875 ms.
findings.actualVsExpected: Both qualifying repetitions pass, but the retained prior miss and small headroom show timing variance.
findings.consequence: A single passing local packet should not be treated as deterministic or universal planner conformance.
findings.priorityRationale: Nonblocking because the unchanged gate passes in both qualifying repetitions and the issue is explicitly retained by the author packet.
findings.recommendedCorrection: Keep the 16 ms budget; measure variance on a named CI runner and a lower-powered device, then profile or reduce planner work if the miss recurs.
findings.verification: Repeat the qualifying workload on the named environments and record all repetitions, including misses, without widening the threshold.

findings.requirement: Selected package bundle budgets remain enforced, while whole-site loading observations must be labeled separately from package-byte qualification.
findings.evidence: The manifest records the homepage shared main chunk at 397606 raw and 112564 served encoded bytes versus 44640 and 15700 at a245c8f.
findings.actualVsExpected: The selected six package rows pass their stated budgets, but the homepage comparison is materially larger and has no applicable T30 whole-site byte threshold.
findings.consequence: Homepage loading/code-splitting cost may regress even while selected package entry-point gates pass.
findings.priorityRationale: Nonblocking because the packet does not mislabel the descriptive comparison as a passed byte budget and preserves the issue explicitly.
findings.recommendedCorrection: Profile a route- or interaction-level lazy boundary for the evaluator/runtime path while retaining the real no-network home proof and current package budgets.
findings.verification: Repeat the site-page observation after the boundary change and compare raw/encoded bytes and functional readiness without replacing the selected bundle gates.

findings.requirement: Installed direct-name consumer evidence should remain independently inspectable and reproducible from retained artifacts.
findings.evidence: The retained consumer lock and bundle report contain exact @aeliqo/core, @aeliqo/runtime and @aeliqo/web 0.1.0 entries, integrity values and package hashes, but their file: resolved paths point to the author worktree /private/tmp/aeliqo-t30-final-revalidation.1sYoht and the three tarballs are not retained in the packet.
findings.actualVsExpected: The lock graph and reported hashes are inspectable, but an independent reviewer cannot reopen the package bytes or independently recompute the hash/integrity pair from this checkout.
findings.consequence: The selected bundle result is supported by the immutable report and lock graph but has weaker artifact-level replayability.
findings.priorityRationale: Nonblocking evidence-quality follow-up; it does not contradict the packet's passing selected rows or source binding.
findings.recommendedCorrection: Retain the exact tarballs or a portable, checksum-bound consumer fixture for future independent review, while preserving the lock's direct-name graph.
findings.verification: Install the retained fixture offline and recompute each package tarball SHA-256 against the lock/report values.

coverage.qualifyingBrowserRuntime: satisfied-by-author-packet; enforced Chromium budgets, bounded large-window geometry and trace phase observations are retained

limitations: This review inspected the immutable author packet and did not rerun its performance, browser, install, publication or network commands; the measurements are author-produced observations.
Measurements cover one Apple M4 Pro/macOS host and one headless Chromium build; no named CI runner, lower-powered device, WebKit/Firefox timing run or field population was measured.

Node and loaded-page first/subsequent observations are reuse conditions within one process or browser fixture. Only standalone/site labels explicitly clear or revalidate browser cache; these are not device-boot or universal cold-start claims.

Visible-input timing stops at an observed DOM mutation. All ordinary Event Timing entries are missing or threshold-censored; the deliberate calibration only verifies that the observation path reports a long event.

Trace phase durations can overlap, the maximum script event encloses aggregate workload evaluation, and zero composite-layer events means no such event was exposed in the trace, not zero compositing cost.

The heap probe is a requested-GC diagnostic from one Chromium process. Empty DOM/listener/resource counters and a responsive positive control do not prove every object is collectible or establish a universal memory budget.
Adverse runtime uses an in-process adapter and does not prove HTTP, socket, proxy, backend cancellation or network capacity.

The selected bundle rows cover installed direct-name entry points and retained module graphs; they do not establish parse, execution, interaction, CSS or whole-site latency. The homepage chunk comparison has no applicable T30 byte ceiling.
The site report's buildId is unknown and its paint/LCP/layout observations are controlled local observations, not field Core Web Vitals or universal input metrics.
No manual assistive-technology certification, provider/model quality, native WebMCP, publication, deployment or backend-capacity claim is made.

verdict.summary: The exact-source T30 author packet is complete, hash-consistent, source- and budget-bound, and supports approval within the inspected scope. No P0 or P1 finding was found. Three explicit P2 follow-ups remain: planner headroom reliability, homepage shared-chunk growth, and independent consumer-tarball reopenability.
